tasks.short: Arrange witness attendance and coordinate when witnesses are called at hearings.

steps.what: Read hearing directions and identify witness attendance requirements.

loop.output: Dates, attendance method, witness requirements, and source passages.
loop.check: Validate dates and identifiers; a paralegal checks each requirement against its source.
loop.stop: One extraction and one repair attempt per document; missing or conflicting requirements return to manual reading.
loop.why_not_simpler: Directions contain variable free text. Structured hearing notices should bypass the loop.

steps.what: Agree the witness list and attendance approach with the lawyer.
Exchange availability and attendance details with witnesses.
Prepare witness notices using approved wording and hearing details.
Check formal notices and approve their issue.
Issue approved notices and track acknowledgements or required service evidence.
Confirm attendance and coordinate the witness call with hearing staff.

tasks.design: Configure the {WORKFLOW}, {EMAIL}, and {CALENDAR} to collect availability, track attendance, and send approved logistical messages. A bounded reader extracts hearing requirements into a case record in the {DOCS}; deterministic templates generate notices, whose issue requires lawyer approval and the correct service channel.
tasks.previous_blocker: Changing hearing directions, separate calendars, and service requirements made coordination awkward. Attendance decisions and formal notices also needed legal supervision.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing scheduling and approval features handle routine coordination. AI-assisted coding reduces the effort of connecting records and templates; bounded extraction helps with free-text directions.
tasks.still_hard: Distressed or reluctant witnesses, last-minute hearing changes, and valid service remain difficult. National procedural rules determine who may summon or call witnesses.
tasks.human_edge: A person notices hesitation, reassures witnesses without coaching testimony, and responds to hearing staff in real time.

ambition.what: A pre-hearing attendance readiness report showing missing confirmations and unresolved access needs.

tasks.altitude: The paralegal spends less time chasing replies and more time resolving attendance obstacles. They can adjust logistics within lawyer-approved limits; witness selection and formal procedural decisions remain with the lawyer.

reach.task: Prepare a source-backed witness chronology for hearing preparation.
reach.learn: Evidence relevance, hearing procedure, and the boundary between logistical support and testimony coaching.

evidence.claim: Availability collection, template filling, reminders, and acknowledgement tracking can use deterministic workflows.
Libra offers legal drafting and review. This supports document assistance, not proof of automated witness coordination.
GDPR Article 28 requires an appropriate processor contract where an external provider processes personal data on the organisation's behalf.

assumptions: This is occasional litigation support within a European company of 200 to 2,000 staff.
The paralegal acts under a lawyer's instructions; hearing staff control the courtroom call where required.
Routine availability messages can use preapproved wording and contain minimal case information.
The time split allocates more effort to email coordination than the weak mail prior suggests.
Build ranges cover one hearing workflow using existing systems and exclude unpredictable consultation or supplier delays.
unknowns: The jurisdictions, hearing types, and legally valid service channels.
Whether the company or an external lawyer manages witness attendance.
Available calendar access, witness contact permissions, and case record interfaces.
Required employee consultation under national rules and whether usage data could monitor staff.
research_questions: Which national procedural rules distinguish attendance invitations, summonses, and formal service?
Can hearing notices supply structured dates and identifiers, removing the extraction loop?
new_work: Check extracted requirements against hearing directions.
Resolve non-responses, changed dates, and inaccessible attendance arrangements.
Maintain notice templates and service-channel rules.
Check failed deliveries and keep permissioned attendance records.

tasks.short: Review property closing evidence and help parties resolve disputes under legal supervision.

steps.what: Collect the transaction documents and parties' stated concerns.
Retrieve current property registry records using the property's identifiers.
Compare title documents, registry entries, ownership details, and restrictions.

loop.input: Title documents, registry records, and property identifiers.
loop.output: Source-linked ownership and restriction fields for deterministic comparison.
loop.check: Match identifiers, names, dates, and amounts; a person checks every extracted restriction against the original.
loop.stop: One extraction and one repair attempt per document; unreadable pages or unmatched fields enter the exception queue.
loop.why_not_simpler: Historical deeds contain free-text restrictions. Structured registry fields should use direct comparisons.

steps.what: Prepare a discrepancy brief with supporting passages and missing documents.
Assess legal significance and agree the permitted negotiation position.
Help parties clarify issues and record possible settlement terms.
Reconcile closing figures and assemble the closing packet.
Review the closing packet and authorise its release.
Send the authorised closing packet and retain delivery evidence.

tasks.design: A case record in the {WORKFLOW} links documents in the {DOCS} to authorised registry queries through the {GOV_PORTAL}. A bounded extraction loop supplies source-linked fields for deterministic comparisons and closing calculations; the {EMAIL} releases only the packet version approved by the lawyer.
tasks.previous_blocker: Registry access, scanned deeds, and closing figures lived in separate places. Legal significance and disputed terms could not be reduced to reliable checklist rules.
tasks.enabler_now: Structured identifiers and repeatable calculations support deterministic checks. Bounded document extraction and faster integration development reduce preparation effort without changing legal authority.
tasks.still_hard: Ambiguous restrictions, incomplete title history, and contested facts require legal judgement. Binding arbitration, conveyancing authority, and registration requirements depend on national rules and the appointed professionals.
tasks.human_edge: The lawyer assesses enforceability and risk. The paralegal helps parties explain concerns and preserves an accurate record of what remains unresolved.

ambition.what: An early closing-readiness review before the company commits to a transaction timetable.

tasks.altitude: The paralegal spends more of the week investigating exceptions and coordinating missing evidence. They can prioritise evidence requests and recommend escalation; settlement commitments and closing release remain with authorised decision-makers.

reach.task: Prepare alternative ways to satisfy a disputed closing condition.
reach.learn: Property rights, contractual remedies, evidence provenance, and the limits of delegated negotiation.

evidence.claim: Structured comparisons, closing arithmetic, document checklists, and release controls can use deterministic code.
Kadaster AkteAI combines models and rules to extract deed data. This supports extraction feasibility, not automated dispute resolution.
Kadaster's historical-deed processing flags easements for human confirmation.
Qualia Clear drafts preliminary title exams and proposes curative tasks in the US title context.
The AEGIS Land Title vendor case reports about 10 to 20 commitments daily and a full audit of each file; no period is given.
EU AI Act Annex III includes relevant justice uses when performed for a court or ADR body; ordinary corporate legal support is not automatically covered by that category.

assumptions: The company occasionally acquires, sells, or disputes rights in property.
The paralegal supports negotiation and closing; they do not independently make a binding arbitral award.
Registry records can be obtained through a permitted interface or authorised structured exports.
A spreadsheet currently reconciles closing figures; registry searching itself uses a system.
Build ranges cover a pilot for one jurisdiction and document family; external professional fees are excluded.
unknowns: The applicable property jurisdiction and required notarial or conveyancing involvement.
Whether formal arbitration is actually part of this role and who has authority to decide.
Registry access rights, charges, export formats, and freshness requirements.
The closing document types, approval thresholds, and settlement authority.
Whether processing is on behalf of a court or ADR body.
Required employee consultation under national rules.
research_questions: Which registry fields and deed exchanges are available in structured form?
Which closing conditions can be mechanically checked in the selected jurisdiction?
Does any proposed deployment fall within the EU AI Act's court or ADR use category?
new_work: Confirm extracted ownership and restriction passages.
Investigate mismatches and missing registry evidence.
Maintain jurisdiction-specific closing templates and calculation rules.
Control approved packet versions and recipient permissions.
Monitor registry interface changes and extraction failures.

tasks.short: Compile an estate asset inventory and support defensible property valuations.

steps.what: Request asset evidence from the estate representative and relevant custodians.
Record reported assets, ownership, balances, and supporting document references.

loop.input: Asset statements, ownership documents, and item lists.
loop.output: Asset records with owner, reported value, currency, date, and source location.
loop.check: Validate types and totals; check ownership, valuation dates, and every material amount against the source.
loop.stop: One extraction and one repair attempt per document; conflicting ownership or amounts require manual entry.
loop.why_not_simpler: Evidence arrives in varied free-text documents. Structured statements should be imported directly.

steps.what: Verify property ownership and account balances against authorised records.
Inspect accessible property and record condition, identity, and missing items.
Agree valuation dates, evidence standards, and the need for specialist appraisals.
Assess valuation evidence and specialist reports against the agreed basis.
Consolidate the inventory and obtain approval of the final version.

tasks.design: A permissioned asset register in the {WORKFLOW} links each holding to evidence in the {DOCS}, with authorised imports from the {BANK} and {GOV_PORTAL}. A bounded reader proposes fields from documents, while deterministic checks detect duplicates and calculate totals; final inventory approval stays with the lawyer.
tasks.previous_blocker: Asset evidence arrived in inconsistent documents and valuations used different dates or ownership assumptions. Physical condition and specialist judgement were never suitable for simple automation.
tasks.enabler_now: A small records app can preserve evidence, dates, currencies, and exceptions without repeated spreadsheet assembly. Bounded extraction reduces transcription effort rather than supplying unsupported valuations.
tasks.still_hard: Hidden assets, disputed ownership, illiquid holdings, and unusual personal property need investigation. Specialist appraisals and national succession or tax rules remain expensive.
tasks.human_edge: A person assesses physical condition, notices incomplete disclosure, and distinguishes a reported price from a defensible valuation.

ambition.what: A pre-meeting estate liquidity and missing-evidence report.

tasks.altitude: The paralegal spends less time transcribing statements and more time investigating ownership and valuation gaps. They can prioritise evidence collection and recommend specialist appraisal; legal and tax conclusions remain with qualified advisers.

reach.task: Prepare an asset liquidity and ownership-restriction brief for estate planning.
reach.learn: Valuation bases, succession terminology, liquidity limits, and the separation of factual support from legal or tax advice.

evidence.claim: Asset registers, duplicate checks, dated values, inventory templates, and arithmetic can use deterministic technology.
Legora offers legal drafting and review. The digest does not establish automated estate valuation.
Kadaster demonstrates deed extraction with human confirmation of flagged easements; this is adjacent evidence for document handling.
An external processor handling personal asset evidence needs an appropriate GDPR Article 28 contract.

assumptions: Estate planning is uncommon in a general corporate legal team. This describes the task where an estate, fiduciary, or private-client remit exists.
The paralegal supports appraisal and commissions qualified specialists where required.
Asset holders have authorised access to statements and registry records.
Currency conversions use an approved rate source and valuation date.
Build ranges cover a limited asset register and existing authorised sources, excluding specialist appraisal fees and elapsed appointment time.
unknowns: Whether estate planning is actually performed by this company's legal team.
Asset classes, estate jurisdictions, and the required valuation standard.
Access rights to bank and registry information.
Who may commission appraisals and approve the inventory.
Required retention periods and employee consultation under national rules.
research_questions: Which asset classes require independent or formally qualified appraisals under the applicable national rules?
Which statement formats can be imported without a model?
What evidence supports the chosen valuation date and currency conversion basis?
new_work: Review extracted asset records and source references.
Resolve duplicates, ownership conflicts, and stale balances.
Maintain asset categories and valuation-date checks.
Track missing appraisals and preserve valuation provenance.
Review access permissions and evidence retention.

tasks.short: Maintain current legal reference sources, subscriptions, and any retained print volumes.

steps.what: Check library catalogue holdings, subscriptions, and renewal dates.
Compare supplier edition notices with recorded holdings.
Decide which references to retain, replace, renew, or discontinue.
Place approved renewal and supplement orders.
Replace print supplements, remove superseded pages, and shelve retained volumes.
Copy completed library updates into a separate local tracking workbook.
Verify licensed reference access and flag missing or stale editions in the catalogue.

tasks.design: Configure the library catalogue in the {OTHER} to hold edition identifiers, renewal dates, and update status, then connect approved purchases through the {PROCUREMENT}. Deterministic comparisons process edition notices from the {EMAIL}, remove duplicate tracking in the {SPREADSHEET}, and produce an exception view; retained print updates remain physical work.
tasks.previous_blocker: Supplier notices, purchase records, and local tracking were disconnected. Print handling was mixed with monitoring, making the whole task appear manual.
tasks.enabler_now: Catalogue configuration and small integrations can centralise edition and subscription metadata. No model is needed when notices contain stable identifiers; irregular notices can remain exceptions.
tasks.still_hard: Supplier metadata may be incomplete, and licences can restrict automated access. Current editions do not by themselves establish which law applies to an earlier event.
tasks.human_edge: A lawyer judges coverage needs and historical relevance. A person safely updates retained print material and resolves uncertain supplier records.

ambition.what: A legal-source coverage gap report for planned entries into new jurisdictions.

tasks.altitude: The paralegal spends less time checking notices and copying logs, and more time resolving source-access and coverage gaps. They can prioritise missing references within the approved coverage plan; subscription spending and legal coverage decisions retain their existing approval rights.

reach.task: Prepare a reference coverage brief for a new jurisdiction or legal topic.
reach.learn: Source authority, historical versions, licence limits, and the team's planned legal needs.

evidence.claim: Catalogue fields, renewal reminders, edition comparisons, and duplicate-log removal can use configuration and deterministic code.
The digest's legal research benchmark reports errors on over 17% of tested queries; catalogue currency should not be treated as validated legal advice.
In the Netherlands, employee monitoring arrangements may require works council consent under WOR Article 27; this design does not need individual output tracking.

assumptions: A mid-size corporate legal team primarily uses licensed digital references and retains a small print collection.
The library catalogue is a library-management category represented by the {OTHER}.
A separate local update workbook duplicates catalogue information and can be removed.
Edition identifiers are available for routine notices; unparseable notices receive manual review.
The digital emphasis differs from the prior's large in-person share; retained print work remains manual.
Build ranges cover existing catalogue and procurement access, including consultation assessment; reference subscription costs are excluded.
unknowns: Whether a maintained print library or duplicate update workbook exists.
The catalogue's configuration options and supplier metadata interfaces.
Licence restrictions on automated access checks.
The required historical holdings and legal coverage priorities.
Purchasing authority and any employee consultation required under national rules.
research_questions: Can suppliers provide structured edition and renewal metadata?
Which retained print sources have acceptable licensed digital equivalents?
How should historical editions be labelled so they remain available without appearing current?
new_work: Resolve unrecognised edition notices and broken source access.
Maintain supplier identifiers and catalogue mappings.
Record completion of retained print updates in the catalogue.
Maintain a single update record after retiring the duplicate workbook.

role.altitude: The paralegal's week shifts toward evidence quality, exceptions, and practical support for people involved in legal matters. They gain bounded authority to prioritise evidence requests and logistics; legal advice, binding settlements, and formal procedural authority remain with authorised professionals.
reach: Prepare source-backed witness chronologies for a lawyer's hearing preparation.
Develop evidence-backed options for disputed closing conditions.
Prepare estate liquidity and ownership briefs where estate work is genuinely within scope.
Identify legal reference coverage gaps for planned jurisdiction changes.
skills_to_grow: Document extraction review and exception handling.
Registry access, confidentiality, and GDPR responsibilities.
National procedural boundaries and effective communication with witnesses and parties.
role.ambitious_version: A legal readiness service gives lawyers early visibility of attendance obstacles, missing closing evidence, unsupported asset values, and reference coverage gaps. It uses permissioned records, deterministic checks, and small reviewed extraction loops; professional decisions and sensitive conversations remain human.
